Brief facts, leading to filing of the present appeal, before this Court, may be summed up, as under:
The Government of Himachal Pradesh has issued notification under Section 4 of the Act, on 15.11.2006, for acquisition of land, comprised in khasra Nos. 296/285/275/1 measuring 0-10 biswas situated in revenue Village Neri Jagela, Tehsil Rajgarh,

The notification issued under Section 4 of the Act was given wide publicity, as per the mandate of the Act, and thereafter, proceedings under Sections 6 and 7 of the Act were conducted and ultimately award was passed, vide award bearing No. 1 of 2006, dated (
2024:HHC:3050 ) 18.11.2008.

The Land Acquisition Collector has assessed the market value of the acquired land as Rs.
90,000/- per bigha.

In addition to this, other statutory .
benefits have also been given to petitioner Anokhi Ram.

4.2 Since, the petitioner was not satisfied with the market value of the acquired land, assessed by the Land Acquisition Collector, as such, reference petition, under Section 18 of the Act, was filed before the Land Acquisition Collector, with a request to forward the same to the learned District Judge, for adjudication.

In this regard, petitioner has also pointed out the commercial potentiality of the acquired land.
In addition to this, petitioner Anokhi Ram has also asserted the fact that the statutory benefits have not been given to him.

Although, it has also been .
pleaded that possession of the acquired land was taken in the year 1963, but, according to him, the land was acquired later on.
As such, he has sought the amount on account of use and occupation charges from the respondents.

4.5 to On the basis of above facts, a prayer has been made to assess the market value of the acquired land, by taking into consideration the commercial potentiality of the same, as highlighted, in the reference petition.
5. When, put to notice, respondents have contested the reference petition by taking the preliminary objection that the petition is time barred.
5.1 On merits, the factum of acquisition of land has not been admitted.

It is the specific stand of the respondents that the market value of the acquired ( 2024:HHC:3050 ) land, has properly been assessed by the learned Land Acquisition Collector, after considering the commercial potentiality of the acquired land.

With regard to the factual position, qua the fact that the possession of the land was taken in the year 1963, it has been pleaded by the respondents that the petitioner and his predecessors had orally donated the land in question to the respondents- Department and has consented to construct the check post.
5.3 Thus, a prayer has been made to dismiss the reference petition.

In such situation, the question which arises for determination, before this Court, is whether any amount can be given to the petitioner, as use and occupation charges of the acquired land,
possession of which was taken by the respondents, in the year 1963?
18.

The answer to the said question is in negative, as the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in case titled as,
Union of India versus Budh Singh & others, ( 2024:HHC:3050 ) reported in (1995) 6 Supreme Court Cases 233, has held that the Act is a self contained code and common law principles of justice, equity and good conscience .
are not applicable.

sentences.text:
Relevant paragraphs 3. 4 and 5 of the said judgment are reproduced as under:
"3.

The only question that arises for decision is whether the respondents-owners of the lands are entitled to interest at 18% per annum from March 15, 1963, the date on which possession was initially taken, till November 15, 1984, preceding the date on which the notification under s.4(1) was published.

It is a jurisdictional issue and the finding in this behalf touches and trenches into the jurisdictional power of the court,
acting under the Act regarding award of interest.
The payment of interest under the Act is squarely covered by the provisions of the Act.
The Government, while exercising its power of eminent domain, are entitled to have the notification under s.4 (1) published in the State Gazette.
They are also entitled, in case of urgency, to exercise the power under s.17(4) of the Act and thereon declaration under s.6 published and would issue notice to the owner of the land under s.9.
On expiry of 15 days thereof, the Government is entitled to take possession from the owner.
The award would be made under S.11 thereafter.
In case urgency clause under s.17(4) was not invoked, the procedure of inquiry under s.5A shall be gone through and thereafter declaration under S.6 be made.
The declaration gives conclusiveness to the public purpose.

After conducting an inquiry in Chapter III of the Act, the Land (
2024:HHC:3050 ) Acquisition officer makes the award under S.11 and gives notice to owner under S.12(2) and he is entitled to take possession from the owner of the land under s.16 and on deposit of the compensation makes payment thereof under .
S.31 of the Act.

In case, after taking possession, if the amount is not paid, the provision is made for payment of interest under S.34 of the Act which reads thus:
"34. Payment of interest when the amount of such compensation is not paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, the Collector shall pay the amount awarded with interest thereon at the rate of nine per centum per annum from the time of so taking possession until it shall have been so paid or r deposited."
4.

Under the proviso after the Amendment Act, if the amount is not paid before one year from the date on which possession is taken, interest at the rate of fifteen per centum per annum shall be payable from the date of expiry of the said period of one year on the amount of compensation or part thereof which has not been paid or deposited before the date of such expiry.

sentences.text: The other provision relevant for this purpose is S.28 of the Act, which empowers the reference court or the High Court for awarding interest on the enhanced compensation from the date of taking possession till date of payment as referred to hereinbefore.

Thus, it could be seen that the statute covers the entire field of operation of the liability of the State to make payment of interest and entitlement thereof by the owner when land has been ( 2024:HHC:3050 ) taken over and possession in consequence thereof, the land owner was deprived of the enjoyment thereof, the land owner was deprived of the enjoyment thereof.

Thus, it could be seen that the Court has no power to impose .
any condition to pay interest in excess of the rate and manner prescribed by the statute as well as for a period anterior to the publication of s.4(1) notification under the Act.

The parameter for initiation of the proceedings is the publication of the notification under s. 4(1) of the Act in the State Gazette or in an appropriate cases in District Gazette as per the local amendments.
But the condition precedent is publication of the notification under s.4(1) in the appropriate gazette.
That would give legitimacy to the State to take possession of the land in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
Any possession otherwise would not be considered to be possession taken under the Act.

In fact, a situation has been envisaged under s.48(2) of the Act, namely, that when proceedings under the Act were initiated and in the mid- stream the proceedings were dropped, the owner who has been deprived of the enjoyment of the property, the statute prescribes the remedy of determination of the amount of compensation due to the owner for the damages suffered by the owner in consequence of the notice of the proceedings under the Act.
The statute also imposes liability on the state to reimburse the costs incurred by the owner to defend the proceedings under the Act.
The Act is a self contained code and common law principles of justice, equity and good conscience cannot be extended in awarding interest, contrary to the provisions of the statute."
19. The notification, issued under Section 4 of the Act, in the present case, was issued on 15.11.2006.

Admittedly, all the four sale deeds, which .
have been relied upon by the petitioners, as exemplar sale deeds, were executed prior to issuance of notification, under Section 4 of the Act.

20. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ravinder Narain versus Union of India, reported in 2003(2)
Apex Court Judgments 306 (S.C.) has formulated certain guidelines, which have to be kept in mind,
while assessing the market value. Para-9 of the judgment is reproduced as under:
"9.

Applying the principles of Ravinder Narain's case (supra), in the present case, this Court is of the view that sale deed, Ext. PW1/B, which was .
executed on 29.7.2004, can be treated as exemplar sale deed
. By way of said sale deed, 2 biswas of land in village Neri Jagela, where, the acquired land is situated, was sold for a sum of Rs. 60,000/-.
Meaning 30,000/- per biswa.

22.
The next question, which arises for determination, before this Court is as to whether any deduction is liable to be made on the value of 1 biswa of land, as per sale deed, Ext. PW1/B?
The answer to this question is in negative, as acquired land is also a small piece of land, measuring 10 biswas.

Thus, market value of the acquired land is, assessed as Rs.
3,00,000/- (Rs. 6,00,000/- per bigha).
23.

In view of the discussions made hereinabove, this Court is of the considered opinion that the (
2024:HHC:3050 ) learned Reference Court has wrongly assessed the market value of the acquired land as Rs. 86,437.50/-
for 10 biswas of land and the same is held to be Rs.
.
3,00,000/-, alongwith statutory relief, as awarded by the learned Reference Court.
24.
No other point has been urged or argued.
25. In view of above, the present appeal is allowed, in the aforesaid terms,and the award passed by the learned Reference Court, is modified accordingly.
26. The pending application(s), if any, are also disposed of.
